title: Ex Line Ranges
intro: Ex commands work on line numbers, so you don't have to move the cursor first. `:3d` deletes line 3 and `:2,4d` deletes lines 2 through 4. `.` means the current line and `$` the last one, so `:.,$d` deletes from here to the end. The same ranges work in front of `:s`, so a substitution only touches those lines.
summary: Delete and replace by line number without moving.

exercises.instruction: Delete line 3 without moving: type `:3d` and press `Enter`.
hints: `:` opens the command line; the number is the line to act on.

exercises.instruction: Delete lines 2 to 4 in one command: `:2,4d` + `Enter`.
Everything from the cursor line to the end is junk: `:.,$d` + `Enter`.
hints: `.` is the current line and `$` is the last line.

exercises.instruction: Delete every line from 2 to the end of the file: `:2,$d` + `Enter`.
hints: `$` works as the end of a range from any line number.

exercises.instruction: Replace `var` with `let`, but only on lines 2 and 3: `:2,3s/var/let/` + `Enter`.
hints: A range in front of `:s` limits which lines it touches.

exercises.instruction: Delete lines 3 and 4 without moving the cursor.
Rename `foo` to `bar` on lines 3 and 4 only, every occurrence on each line.
